newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Drought-hit Ethiopia calls for urgent food aid.
newsitem.headline: Drought-hit Ethiopia calls for urgent food aid.

text.p: Ethiopia appealed on Friday for 181,000 tonnes of food aid to be urgently sent to feed more than three million people hit by drought in the north and south this year.
The state Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Commission (DPPC) said donor response to previous appeals for the aid were very poor and the number of people hit by drought could rise.
It said the failure of short rains from March to May known as Belg had hit some 1.4 million people in northern Amhara region alone and other regions including Tigray and the south.
"The situation is bad in some parts of Ethiopia and the poor Belg rains will increase the need for food aid," said U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) spokeswoman Brenda Barton in Nairobi.
"There is an urgent need for food aid and WFP is finalising its analysis of the outcome of the Belg harvest," she added.

The DPPC in June estimated 3,418,190 people would need 329,451 tonnes of food aid this year. Aid agencies said taking into account aid in the pipeline there remained a shortfall of 88,753 tonnes of food and the food gap was expected to widen.
U.N. missions in June to various regions reported the Belg crop was likely to be the worst in three years. The Belg rains generally started late in Ethiopia and were poor, short and uneven.
Grain prices in Ethiopia rose by 33 percent from mid-April to June and fertiliser sales this year by the end of June were estimated at half what they were at the same time the previous year.
Ethiopia suffered a catastrophic famine in 1984, prompting the "Live Aid" rock concert which was beamed live around the world and helped raise millions of dollars to ease the disaster.
